strongest_angle: Explore how the 2026 Super El Niño weather pattern and heavy winter downpours triggered the largest floral bloom in decades across nearly 7,000 square miles of Chile's Atacama Desert.

key_facts.fact: Nearly 7,000 square miles of Chile's Atacama Desert were carpeted in wildflowers after heavy rains brought by the El Niño super cycle.
Heavy winter rains brought by the El Niño super cycle caused flash floods in Copiapó, Chile, with some areas receiving the heaviest rainfall since records began in the 1950s.

AP News reported on October 1, 2026, that Chile's Atacama Desert is covered in flowers due to heavy rains from the El Niño weather pattern earlier this year, with the phenomenon expected to last until November.
Live Science reported on October 2, 2026, that an exceptionally strong El Niño awakened millions of seeds and bulbs in Chile's Atacama Desert.
